selected_result: Blanchard–Higham–Mary equation (3.7): backward-error bound for FABsum with recursive block sums and pairwise accumulation

bibliographic_source.title: A Class of Fast and Accurate Summation Algorithms

paper_locations.anchor: Blocked summation, arbitrary-length pairwise summation, FABsum algorithm, and n divisible by b
Per-input backward-error representation with first-order coefficient b-1+ceil(log2(n/b))

task_clarification: Formalize equation (3.7) as a specialization of FABsum: for n=k*b with positive k and b, compute each size-b block by recursive working-precision summation, then use an arbitrary-length pairwise sum of the k computed block totals at the same precision.

For every vector of n real inputs, represent the computed value as the exact sum of x_i*(1+mu_i), with a uniform bound whose first-order coefficient is b-1+ceil(log2(k)). An explicit finite-u gamma-form bound that implies the paper's first-order statement is acceptable as a strengthening if it preserves the full source domain and algorithm.
The paper includes b=1 and b=n as special cases; do not restrict k to powers of two or omit either case.
scope_constraints: Cover arbitrary positive k and b for which the standard gamma guards hold; pairwise accumulation may use exact zero padding, but it must not narrow the number of blocks to a power of two.
The conclusion is a backward-error representation for every input, not merely a forward absolute-error bound or a bound for one-signed inputs.
Use the actual recursive block and pairwise accumulation algorithms; do not assume an abstract bound on the already-composed FABsum as a hypothesis.
The asymptotic O(u^2) remainder is not itself a numeric inequality at arbitrary fixed u; any finite-u strengthening needs its exact coefficient and validity assumptions.
